Fixes https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/31256

Some files had to be split because the features they test are only available in .NET Core.
pr_comments: There are 852 test failures in the System.IO.FileSystem.Tests on .NET Framework ;)

>  _There are 852 test failures in the System.IO.FileSystem.Tests on .NET Framework ;)_

Strange. I fixed the ones I hit locally (they only were features unavailable in Framework). I didn't hit any regressions. I'll investigate.

Edit: Ah! They are happening in x86. I didn't test that locally.
This will take a while to address. I'll close the PR for now.
Force pushing prevents me from reopening this PR. I'll have to submit a new one.

issue_context.title: Add back netfx test run in System.IO.FileSystem
issue_context.body:
Per https://github.com/dotnet/corefx/pull/41452#issuecomment-544650139

If instead we decide to close this issue, please delete the netfx-specific tests added in the above PR.
comments: Triage: We definitely want to do this to make sure we're catching unintentional regressions and document where we intentionally change behavior from .NET Framework.

Per [this comment](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/pull/33063#issuecomment-617416082), we won't be re-enabling the tests for .NET Framework.
We would still have to submit a PR to remove the Framework specific tests from FileSystem.

> We definitely want to do this to make sure we're catching unintentional regressions and document where we intentionally change behavior from .NET Framework.

Just to address this: our existing tests should cover this.  When we make a change to a test case we should note that it corresponds to a behavior change that's may be a breaking change.  We don't need to run the tests against .NETFramework in order to catch that.

If we do decide to write new tests that cover API that exists on .NETFramework it would make sense for the initial author of those tests to run them against .NETFramework to understand their differences.

review_comments: I'm assuming all of the code that was moved between files wasn't modified at all and thus I don't need to review it, correct?
Correct, no change aside from the "partial" keyword.
